sections.h2: How do owners usually sell a house in Buffalo Grove?
sections.html:
Most Buffalo Grove owners list with an agent, because the village's housing market is built around mortgage-financed buyers and long-tenured owners. A direct sale to a cash buyer is the alternative when a house needs work or the closing date matters more than the top price.

The village adds one local step to every route. Buffalo Grove sells its own real estate transfer stamps, in person only, and holds them back if water or other village debts are unpaid. A seller who plans for that stamp early avoids a delayed closing.

  • Agent listing: more showings, more time, and the buyer's financing to wait on.
  • Owner sale: saves the commission, but you handle disclosures, the deed and the stamp visit.
  • Cash purchase: fewer contingencies and a closing set by you, usually at a lower price than a retail sale.

sections.h2: Which county is a Buffalo Grove house in?
sections.html:
Buffalo Grove is split by Lake Cook Road: the northern part, about three-quarters of the village, is in Vernon Township in Lake County, and the southern part is in Wheeling Township in Cook County. The village's own transfer tax page says that anyone changing the property record with Cook or Lake County needs a stamp.

So the deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division or with Lake County, depending on the parcel. Cook County Clerk's recordings office hours run 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the last customer is accepted at 4:45 p.m. Property tax bills, exemptions and appeals also follow the county, so check which assessor and treasurer cover your parcel.

The split shows up in services too. The Indian Trails Public Library District serves the Cook County part, and the Vernon Area Public Library District serves most of the Lake County part.

sections.h2: What does a Buffalo Grove transfer stamp cost and require?
sections.html:
The village charges $3 per $1,000 for its transfer tax, and it will not issue a stamp while water, fines, fees or other debts to the village are outstanding. Stamps can only be bought in person at Village Hall, 50 Raupp Boulevard.

Buffalo Grove transfer stamp requirements, from the Village's Real Estate Transfer Tax page
ItemWhat the Village says
Tax amount$3 per $1,000
Where to buyIn person at Village Hall
Before you goCall Finance at 847-459-2500 or email bgfinance@vbg.org for a property check
DocumentsVillage transfer tax form signed by seller and buyer, PTAX or MyDec form, and deed or latest tax bill
Details requiredClosing date and forwarding address
OrdinanceChapter 3.44 of the municipal code

Exempt examples include a seller that is a unit of government and a re-titling between an individual and a trust. All debts must still be paid before an exempt stamp is issued. Bring the stamp to closing so the county can record the new deed.

sections.h2: What do water and sewer bills mean for a Buffalo Grove closing?
sections.html:
Water and sewer balances must be paid before the Village will issue a stamp, so a final bill needs to be settled ahead of closing. The Village's rate page lists $7.14 per 1,000 gallons for water and $1.77 per 1,000 gallons for sewer as of January 2026, a combined $8.91.

Lake County residents also pay a sanitary sewer pass-through fee of $5.26 per 1,000 gallons as of December 2025. If your house is on the Lake County side, that line item appears on your bill and will not appear for Cook County neighbors across Lake Cook Road.

The property check from the Finance Department is the quickest way to learn what you owe. Ask for the figure a few days before the closing date.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Buffalo Grove housing?
sections.html:
Census Bureau figures put the median owner-occupied home value in Buffalo Grove at $412,300, and 79.8 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners. The 2020 census count was 43,212, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 42,812, a decline of 0.9 percent from the 2020 base.

  • Median household income: $129,395 (2020-2024).
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and older: 68.6 percent.
  • Median gross rent: $2,037.
  • Mean commute: 26.3 minutes.
  • Share in the same house a year earlier: 88.6 percent.

The numbers describe an established village where population has been flat for years. Pricing a house against recent sales on your own street matters more than the village-wide median, which blends very different subdivisions.

sections.h2: How did Buffalo Grove grow, and where do its residents work?
sections.html:
Buffalo Grove incorporated in 1958 with 164 residents after a builder wanted his new development out from under Cook County planners. Developers filled the farmland with single-family houses, and the 1970s brought roughly 80 percent growth, along with home rule status and the village's high schools, park district and libraries.

Wikipedia lists about 20,000 daytime workers in ten million square feet of commercial and industrial space. The 2019 largest employers it names include Siemens Building Technologies, about 1,800 employees, and Plexus Corp. Woodman's Markets, supported by a village tax agreement, anchors retail along Milwaukee Avenue. Buffalo Grove High School and Adlai E. Stevenson High School both opened in the 1970s.

For a seller, the timeline matters because most of the village was platted after the 1950s, so a buyer's inspector will compare your house against subdivisions of the same era.

sections.h2: What local amenities can a seller point to in Buffalo Grove?
sections.html:
Buffalo Grove's Park District runs dozens of recreation facilities. Willow Stream Park is the largest at 54 acres, with sports fields, bike paths and playgrounds, and Mike Rylko Community Park hosts a Sunday farmers market from June to October and the Buffalo Grove Days festival in September.

The Raupp Museum, dedicated in 1979, covers the village's history from the Potawatomi onward. Two golf courses and the Community Arts Center, which opened in 2014, round out the list. Mentioning these in a listing or a conversation with a cash buyer gives context that numbers alone do not.

sections.h2: What state rules sit behind the village stamp?
sections.html:
Illinois imposes its own transfer tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, collected by the county recorder, and counties may add 25 cents per $500. Home rule municipalities such as Buffalo Grove can layer their own tax on top, which is why the village stamp exists.

The buyer and seller also complete the Illinois PTAX-203 transfer declaration, filed with the county where the property sits. The state's paper revenue stamps were scheduled for phase-out by December 31, 2025, after which counties issue electronic stamps, and the Village's own stamp is issued in person at Village Hall.

sections.h2: How does flooding and winter weather affect a Buffalo Grove house?
sections.html:
Buffalo Grove sits in a humid continental climate with about 28.93 inches of precipitation a year, cold snowy winters and hot summers. The village also uses open space for flood control: Buffalo Creek forest preserve functions as flood control, and the Buffalo Grove Golf Course is used as a floodplain.

Buyers near those areas often ask about basement dampness and drainage. Gather any sump pump service records and permits for roof or foundation work, since those papers answer the questions early.

faqs.q: How much is the Buffalo Grove transfer tax?
faqs.a: The Village charges $3 per $1,000. Its Real Estate Transfer Tax page also says the closing date and a forwarding address are required when you buy the stamp.

faqs.q: Can I get a Buffalo Grove transfer stamp online?
faqs.a: No. The Village says stamps can only be obtained in person at Village Hall, 50 Raupp Boulevard, after a property check with the Finance Department at 847-459-2500.

faqs.q: What blocks a stamp from being issued?
faqs.a: Delinquent water charges, outstanding fines or fees, or any other debt owed to the Village. All debts must be paid before even an exempt stamp is issued.

faqs.q: Is Buffalo Grove in Cook County or Lake County?
faqs.a: Both. Lake Cook Road divides the village, with about three-quarters in Lake County's Vernon Township and the rest in Cook County's Wheeling Township. Your parcel determines where the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need a deed to get the stamp?
faqs.a: You need the deed or the most recent tax bill for the property. If you lack the deed, the Cook County Clerk or Lake County recording office can supply a copy.
